llm.reply:
Lynch syndrome is linked in the knowledge graph to a set of genes led by DNA mismatch repair genes [10]. The condition also has several associated clinical studies [1]. Its condition record carries the name Lynch syndrome [7].

## Mismatch Repair Genes

NCBIGene:4292 is mutL homolog 1 [10]. NCBIGene:4436 is mutS homolog 2 [11]. NCBIGene:2956 is mutS homolog 6 [8]. NCBIGene:5395 is PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. NCBIGene:5378 is PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13]. NCBIGene:27030 is mutL homolog 3 [6].

## Other Associated Genes

NCBIGene:4072 is epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. NCBIGene:7048 is transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16]. NCBIGene:999 is cadherin 1 [17]. NCBIGene:4763 is neurofibromin 1 [12]. NCBIGene:6224 is ribosomal protein S20 [15].

## Clinical Studies

One study is Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Another is Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. A third is Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. A fourth is Educational CD-ROM Compared With Standard Informed Consent for Patients With Colorectal Cancer or a Family History of Colorectal Cancer [4]. A fifth is Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Records and Literature

The MedGen record is titled Lynch syndrome [19]. One review is titled Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome [22]. Another is titled Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications [30].

Lynch syndrome is linked in the graph to mismatch repair genes, including NCBIGene:4292, mutL homolog 1 [10]. The linked genes also include NCBIGene:4436, mutS homolog 2 [11]. Another is NCBIGene:2956, mutS homolog 6 [8].

## Causal and associated genes

The PMS family is represented by NCBIGene:5395, PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. The same family also includes NCBIGene:5378, PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13]. NCBIGene:27030, mutL homolog 3, is also linked [6]. Other associated genes are NCBIGene:4072, epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. Further ones are NCBIGene:7048, transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16]. The set also contains NCBIGene:999, cadherin 1 [17]. It includes NCBIGene:4763, neurofibromin 1 [12]. It includes NCBIGene:6224, ribosomal protein S20 [15]. The findings did not include any specific clinical variant records.

## Condition record

The disease record is named Lynch syndrome [7]. The MedGen concept is titled Lynch syndrome [19]. One literature entity is Lynch syndrome I (site-specific colonic cancer) [20]. Another is Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23]. A third is Lynch Syndrome II [26].

## Clinical trials

One registered study is Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Another is Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. A third is Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. One study is Educational CD-ROM Compared With Standard Informed Consent for Patients With Colorectal Cancer or a Family History of Colorectal Cancer [4]. There is also Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Literature

One review is titled Lynch syndrome. [18] Publication 21508689 is listed [21]. Another paper is Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome. [22] Publication 24468183 is listed [24]. A further one is Lynch Syndrome-Associated Colorectal Cancer. [25] Publication 30134129 is listed [27]. There is also Identification of Lynch Syndrome. [28] Publication 34798986 is listed [29]. The last is Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications. [30]
